source.title: Separate the Wheat from the Chaff: A Post-Hoc Approach to Safety Re-Alignment for Fine-Tuned Language Models
source.authors: Di Wu; Xin Lu; Yan-Yan Zhao; Bing Qin

record.tranche_reason: The study measures safety outcomes after benign task fine-tuning, using its own datasets and MD-Judge safety benchmarks rather than the original study's exact recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper's own SFT results on benign datasets bear on V2. Its harmful fine-tuning experiment mixes 1,000 harmful examples with GSM8K and reports results after applying safety realignment methods, but does not report an untreated harmful-fine-tuned safety result; cited prior findings are not rows. It does not measure response-position KL, compliant prefills, or safety depth.
record.test_reason: Table 1 reports MD-Judge safety scores for Llama-2-7b-chat after full fine-tuning on benign task data (GSM8K, CodeAlpaca-20k, Chinese Alpaca), with Δ against the original model. This bears directly on V2, using a different recipe and judge from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The paper takes fine-tuning's safety loss as motivation, citing prior work and showing it in its SFT baselines. Its main conclusion is that IRR restores safety on harmful-query and jailbreak benchmarks while preserving downstream performance (a Pareto improvement over RESTA and Safe LoRA).
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign task SFT on GSM8K, CodeAlpaca-20k, and Chinese Alpaca, then measures benchmark safety using MD-Judge; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The magnitude of the reported safety reduction differs by fine-tuning dataset: GSM8K and CodeAlpaca-20k show larger reported average harmful-benchmark drops than Chinese Alpaca.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The reported safety metric is a moderator-assessed Safety Score rather than a direct refusal rate. Original-model scores are not provided for individual benchmark components, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. The harmful fine-tuning result lacks an untreated harmful-fine-tuned safety result.
record.rows_left_out: No results under the 60-row limit were omitted. Harmful fine-tuning figure results after IRR or RESTA were not included because they do not report untreated harmful-fine-tuned safety.

untested.parts: Harmful-data mix experiment (Fig. 9, 1,000 BeaverTails pairs + GSM8K, LoRA) reports only post-realignment curves, not the untreated harmful-fine-tuned model's safety.
Carefully selected benign examples; refusal-rate measure (uses MD-Judge harmlessness proportion instead); models other than Llama-2-7b-chat in tabulated form.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
Jailbreak attacks are evaluated only as a post-fine-tuning outcome; there is no prefill or decoding-bypass test of the original model's refusal.
The IRR method removes a Fisher-selected subset of delta parameters, but this is a mitigation-method result and not a test of safety localization.

missing.what: SFT (untreated) safety points for LoRA fine-tuning of Llama-2-7b-chat on the three datasets, harmful and jailbreak benchmarks
SFT safety for Llama-3-8B-Instruct LoRA on MathInstruct versus the original
SFT models show lower safety in Chinese and Vietnamese CATQA than in English

record.verdict_notes: The record's limits_scope label for Chinese Alpaca rested on a likely table typo (Δ 0.90 versus the inferred 9.90); it is dropped. The Safe LoRA row in Table 1(c) is identical to Table 1(a), suggesting further copy errors in the table. The safety metric is the MD-Judge harmless proportion, and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The harmful-data experiment does not report the harmful-fine-tuned model's safety before applying realignment.
Does not test carefully selected benign examples; tests ordinary task datasets. Safety score is a moderation-based safety metric, not a direct refusal rate.
No per-token KL or response-position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-bypass test.
Does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test why safety might be shallow.
Does not test training that deepens safety across response positions or its durability.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-7b-chat, full fine-tuning on GSM8K, CodeAlpaca-20k, or Chinese Alpaca+50K English
relationships.reason: The harmful-benchmark average falls by 19.83, 29.96 and about 9.9 (r4, r14, r24 corrected). The jailbreak average falls by 47.71, 55.92 and 26.75 (r10, r20, r30).
relationships.display_finding: The harmful-benchmark average fell by 19.83, 29.96 and about 9.9, and the jailbreak average by 47.71, 55.92 and 26.75.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Benign SFT on GSM8K and CodeAlpaca-20k
reader_labels.reason: The reported average harmful-benchmark safety scores fall by 19.83 and 29.96, respectively, and average jailbreak safety also falls; see r4, r10, r14, and r20.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Benign SFT on Chinese Alpaca plus 50K English instances
reader_labels.reason: The harmful-benchmark average decreases by only 0.90, a much smaller change than for the other tested datasets; see r24. The average jailbreak score also declines; see r30.
